stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that studied in six short sessions
The group that studied in one long session

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group asked the question with the word 'smashed'
The group asked the question with the word 'contacted'

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that drank caffeinated coffee
The group that drank decaffeinated coffee

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They hypothesized that the number of other people present would affect the reporting of an emergency.

**Participants.** The sample was 80 university students, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

**Results.** The group that waited with four other people: mean time before reporting (s) = 196. The group that waited alone: mean time before reporting (s) = 58. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 90 students were randomly assigned to study 40 vocabulary words either in six ten-minute sessions on different days or in one sixty-minute session. One month later, the spaced group recalled a mean of 27 words and the single-session group a mean of 16 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** In an experiment, 120 students read a passage and were randomly assigned either to take three practice quizzes or to reread the passage three times. On a test one week later, the quiz group scored a mean of 68 percent and the rereading group 49 percent (p = 0.01).

**Source C.** In a survey of 600 students, 71 percent said that rereading notes was their main study method, and most rated it as highly effective. Only 12 percent said that they regularly tested themselves.

questions.stem: An eighty-year-old reflects on her life and feels that it was meaningful and well lived. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.
Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Correct. Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.

questions.explanation: Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the autonomic nervous system?

options.why: That describes the central nervous system.

options.text: The division of the peripheral nervous system that controls voluntary movement of the skeletal muscles
options.why: That describes the somatic nervous system.

options.text: The division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort
options.why: Correct. This is what the autonomic nervous system means.

options.text: The division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy
options.why: That describes the parasympathetic nervous system.

questions.explanation: The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste?

options.why: Synesthesia is the condition in which stimulating one sense produces an experience in another sense.
Correct. Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.
Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.
Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.

questions.explanation: Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Yuki reads a note with several letters smudged, yet she understands every word because she knows what the sentence should say. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.
The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.
Correct. Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.
Bottom-up processing is perception that starts with the raw sensory input and builds up to a complete picture.

questions.explanation: Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the psychodynamic perspective?

options.text: The view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful
options.why: That describes the evolutionary perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes
options.why: That describes the biological perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement
options.why: That describes the behavioral perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood
options.why: Correct. This is what the psychodynamic perspective means.

questions.explanation: The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: After a study in which participants were misled about its purpose, the researcher explains what was really being studied. Which ethical requirement is this?

options.why: Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.
Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.
Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
Correct. Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.

questions.explanation: Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: One group differed from the other in whether a small request came first
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The two groups differed in compliance with a large request at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The homeowners asked to sign the petition lived on a road where an accident had recently happened
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes amplitude?

options.text: The distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light
options.why: That describes wavelength.

options.text: The coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses
options.why: That describes the cochlea.

options.text: The height of a sound wave, which determines loudness
options.why: Correct. This is what amplitude means.

options.text: The number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch
options.why: That describes frequency.

questions.explanation: Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes gender?

options.text: A person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination
options.why: That describes gender identity.

options.text: The socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman
options.why: Correct. This is what gender means.

options.text: The set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women
options.why: That describes a gender role.

options.text: The direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction
options.why: That describes sexual orientation.

questions.explanation: Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.

questions.stem: Railway tracks in a drawing appear to come together at the horizon, which makes the scene look deep. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.
Correct. Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.
Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.
Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.

questions.explanation: Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.stem: For the past month, Elena has felt hopeless, has lost interest in everything she used to enjoy and sleeps most of the day. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Correct. Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.explanation: Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.

questions.stem: With her eyes closed, Uma can still touch her nose with her fingertip. Which sense makes this possible?

options.why: The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
Correct. Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.explanation: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: A therapist selects a treatment because controlled studies show it works for the client's disorder and it fits the client's preferences. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.
A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.
Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.explanation: Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 90 university students. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: Dan believes that his grades depend on luck and on whether the teacher likes him. Which belief does he hold?

options.why: A self-fulfilling prophecy is an expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true.
An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
Correct. An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.
The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.

questions.explanation: An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: The group on the waiting list
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: A person sees the world entirely in shades of gray because only one type of cone, or none, works. Which condition is this?

options.why: Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.
Correct. Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.explanation: Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the medulla?

options.text: The base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing
options.why: Correct. This is what the medulla means.

options.text: The master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus
options.why: That describes the pituitary gland.

options.text: The network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness
options.why: That describes the reticular activating system.

options.text: The structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning
options.why: That describes the cerebellum.

questions.explanation: The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories?

options.why: Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.
Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
Correct. The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.

questions.explanation: The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase?

options.why: A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.
A longitudinal study is research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period.
Correct. Discontinuous development is the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase.
Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.

questions.explanation: Discontinuous development is the view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase.

questions.stem: After the tone is sounded many times with no food, a dog stops salivating to the tone. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.
Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.
Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.explanation: Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.

questions.stem: Ice cream sales and drownings rise together, but both are caused by hot weather. Which problem does this illustrate?

options.why: A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.
Correct. The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.

questions.explanation: The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.

questions.stem: Since his teens, Vic has lied, stolen and hurt people without feeling any guilt or remorse. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.
Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Correct. Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.

questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: +0.20, +0.28, −0.44, −0.70. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: +0.28 is closer to zero.
+0.20 is closer to zero.
−0.44 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.70 is farthest from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.70 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: Because a job applicant is attractive, the interviewers assume he is also intelligent and honest. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.
Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
Correct. The halo effect is the tendency for one good quality of a person to make us assume they have other good qualities.
A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.

questions.explanation: The halo effect is the tendency for one good quality of a person to make us assume they have other good qualities.

questions.stem: In psychodynamic theory, denial, projection and rationalization are all examples of which of the following?

options.why: A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.
The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
Correct. A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.

questions.explanation: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.

questions.stem: After brain surgery, a patient remembers his past but forgets each new person minutes after meeting them. Which condition does he have?

options.why: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Correct. Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.explanation: Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.stem: Ben always plans ahead, meets every deadline and keeps his desk tidy. He would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.
Correct. Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.

questions.explanation: Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes in-group bias?

options.text: The tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike
options.why: That describes out-group homogeneity bias.

options.text: The tendency to favor the members of one's own group
options.why: Correct. This is what in-group bias means.

options.text: The tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes
options.why: That describes confirmation bias.

options.text: The tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited
options.why: That describes belief perseverance.

questions.explanation: In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.stem: After many months of unrelieved stress, Lia feels worn out and catches one infection after another. Which phase of the general adaptation syndrome is this?

options.why: Correct. The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.
The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.
The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.

questions.explanation: The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.

questions.stem: Receptors in Tia's fingertip detect a pinprick, and a signal travels toward her spinal cord. Which cells carry this incoming signal?

options.why: Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Correct. Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.

questions.explanation: Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes somnambulism?

options.text: A sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams
options.why: That describes REM sleep behavior disorder.

options.text: Sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep
options.why: Correct. This is what somnambulism means.

options.text: A sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep
options.why: That describes narcolepsy.

options.text: A sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings
options.why: That describes sleep apnea.

questions.explanation: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.stem: As a friend walks away, her image on Tom's retina shrinks, but he does not think she is getting smaller. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.

questions.explanation: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.

questions.stem: Hallucinations and delusions are experiences that are present in schizophrenia but absent in healthy functioning. Which kind of symptom are they?

options.why: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
Correct. A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.

questions.explanation: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes autism spectrum disorder?

options.text: The neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness
options.why: That describes attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.

options.text: The neurodevelopmental disorder marked by difficulties with social communication and by repetitive behaviors or narrow interests
options.why: Correct. This is what autism spectrum disorder means.

options.text: The eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise
options.why: That describes bulimia nervosa.

options.text: The eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward
options.why: That describes binge-eating disorder.

questions.explanation: Autism spectrum disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by difficulties with social communication and by repetitive behaviors or narrow interests.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning?

options.why: Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.
Humanity is the category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence.
Correct. Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.explanation: Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.

questions.stem: In a group where everyone else gives an obviously wrong answer about the length of a line, a participant gives the same wrong answer. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.
Correct. Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.
Individualism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits.
Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.

questions.explanation: Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.

questions.stem: A researcher who expects a drug to work smiles more at the patients who receive it and rates their improvement more generously. Which bias is this?

options.why: Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.
Correct. Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.

questions.explanation: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: A woman hears voices commenting on her actions when nobody is there. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
Correct. A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.
Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.explanation: A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 40 laboratory rats. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: Six dots are drawn as three close pairs, and people see three groups rather than six dots. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Correct. Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.

questions.explanation: Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.stem: A five-year-old realizes that his sister will look for her doll where she left it, even though he knows it has been moved. What has he developed?

options.why: Correct. Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.
Conservation is the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes.
Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.
Animism is the belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions.

questions.explanation: Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles?

options.why: Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.
Correct. Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.explanation: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.stem: A three-year-old says 'I runned fast' and 'two foots'. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Correct. Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.

questions.explanation: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.stem: Kim knows that Paris is the capital of France, although she cannot remember when she learned it. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Correct. Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.explanation: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive?

options.why: Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.
Correct. An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.
Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.

questions.explanation: An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: Correct. A negative correlation means the two measures tend to move in opposite directions.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: That would be a positive correlation.

questions.explanation: A negative correlation means the two measures tend to move in opposite directions.

questions.stem: Having just changed her password, Ming keeps typing her old one. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.
The tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon is the temporary inability to retrieve a word that one is sure one knows.
Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.
Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Sample size does not determine the research method.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes reuptake?

options.text: The stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing
options.why: That describes the resting potential.

options.text: The process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse
options.why: Correct. This is what reuptake means.

options.text: The level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire
options.why: That describes the threshold.

options.text: The brief electrical charge that travels down the axon when a neuron fires
options.why: That describes the action potential.

questions.explanation: Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.

questions.stem: Which term refers to the first ejaculation, which marks sexual maturity in boys?

options.why: Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.
Correct. Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.
Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.explanation: Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.

questions.stem: To remember the term 'hippocampus', Sol links it to a hippo on a campus who never forgets his classes. Which technique is he using?

options.why: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Correct. Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.

questions.explanation: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: One group differed from the other in the behavior of an adult model
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: Only the children who watched the aggressive adult had a favorite toy taken away before the free play
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: The two groups differed in aggressive behavior at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: After considering several careers and trying two internships, Nadia commits to becoming a nurse. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.
Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Correct. Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.

questions.explanation: Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that the number of hours of social media use per day causes a change in score on a depression questionnaire?

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: A coach performs a correct free throw slowly so that her players can watch and copy it. The coach is doing which of the following?

options.why: A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.
Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
Correct. Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
Vicarious conditioning is learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior.

questions.explanation: Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes neuroplasticity?

options.text: A recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface
options.why: That describes an EEG.

options.text: A scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow
options.why: That describes an fMRI.

options.text: The condition in which the two hemispheres cannot communicate because the corpus callosum has been cut
options.why: That describes a split brain.

options.text: The brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience
options.why: Correct. This is what neuroplasticity means.

questions.explanation: Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience.

questions.stem: After hours without water, Tom feels an unpleasant tension that pushes him to find a drink. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: Correct. Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.
Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.

questions.explanation: Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.

questions.stem: A toddler who knows the word 'dog' sees a cow for the first time and calls it a dog. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.
Correct. Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.
A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.explanation: Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.

questions.stem: A child's parents and teachers meet regularly and work together. In ecological systems theory, this connection is part of which system?

options.why: The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.
Correct. The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.
The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.
The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.

questions.explanation: The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood?

options.why: Correct. Mood-congruent memory is the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood.
Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.
The testing effect is the finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading.
Context-dependent memory is the improved recall that occurs in the same place where the information was learned.

questions.explanation: Mood-congruent memory is the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood.

questions.stem: Avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Correct. Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.explanation: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the misinformation effect?

options.text: The distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event
options.why: Correct. This is what the misinformation effect means.

options.text: The building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information
options.why: That describes constructive memory.

options.text: The inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned
options.why: That describes source amnesia.

options.text: The increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it
options.why: That describes imagination inflation.

questions.explanation: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the circadian rhythm?

options.text: The sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles
options.why: That describes REM sleep.

options.text: The deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake
options.why: That describes NREM stage 3.

options.text: The body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep
options.why: Correct. This is what the circadian rhythm means.

options.text: The brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling
options.why: That describes NREM stage 1.

questions.explanation: The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a mental set?

options.text: A step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution
options.why: That describes an algorithm.

options.text: The mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior
options.why: That describes executive functions.

options.text: The tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works
options.why: Correct. This is what a mental set means.

options.text: A simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors
options.why: That describes a heuristic.

questions.explanation: A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of the reporting of an emergency

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of the reporting of an emergency.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: The reporting of an emergency was defined as the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. On average, the value was 196 for the group that waited with four other people and 58 for the group that waited alone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 80 university students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The participants who were with other people took longer to report the smoke. (196 compared with 58).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the number of other people present affects the reporting of an emergency. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the number of other people present. The finding illustrates the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: people feel less personal duty to act when others are present.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Which study methods lead to the best long-term learning?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Spacing study sessions and testing oneself lead to better long-term learning than cramming or rereading.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who spread their study over six days recalled 27 of 40 words a month later, compared with 16 for students who studied in one session.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the spacing effect: distributed practice gives repeated chances to encode and consolidate the material, so it is retained longer than with massed practice.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who took practice quizzes scored 68 percent a week later, compared with 49 percent for students who reread the passage.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the testing effect: retrieving information from memory strengthens the memory and its retrieval cues more than rereading does.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
